chunks: Sufficient is Allah and His Word as perfection.

There is no god but Allah, alone, without partner; to Him belongs the dominion and to Him belongs the praise; He gives life and causes death, and He is the Ever-Living who does not die. The remaining [goodness] is better for your Lord, and for security after certainty.

key_terms.لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ: Without partner (denying any associate in divinity)
key_terms.يُحْيِي وَيُمِيتُ: He gives life and causes death

ai.seo_question: What is the core declaration of divine unity and eternal life in Shia creedal texts?
ai.summary: Recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq in *Kamal al-Din*, this hadith functions as a foundational creedal statement for Twelver Shi'ism, linking Allah's absolute sovereignty (Mulkiyyah) directly to the perfection of His divine speech. It underscores that ultimate security (Aman) and enduring goodness (Khayr) are exclusive to Allah, reinforcing the concept of divine self-sufficiency (Al-Ghani) against human contingency. This summary serves to anchor the believer's theological certainty in the attributes of the Divine before delving into the specific proofs of Imamate.
